tool.help:
**What this tool does**
**Focaloop GeneLoop** predicts protein-coding genes, alternatively spliced transcripts, and non-coding RNAs on eukaryotic genome assemblies. Instead of downloading and aligning 100% of every RNA-seq library up front, it combines homology and deep-learning seed models with adaptive RNA-seq streaming that focuses alignment effort on unresolved genes and stops automatically once splice-junction discovery converges.
-----
**How it works**
1. **Initial homology and deep-learning seed:** Aligns related-species proteins (`miniprot`) and, when deep-learning weights are available, runs Tiberius gene prediction. Well-supported multi-exon genes with intact reading frames and consistent introns are locked in, while uncertain, single-exon, or unsupported loci remain open for transcript evidence. 2. **Unique-sequence abundance filter:** Builds a fast filter covering only sequences that appear **once** in the genome inside already-converged coding genes (plus mitochondrial/plastid and rRNA contigs). Skipping reads from already-resolved unique housekeeping genes saves alignment time while protecting multi-copy gene families and paralogs from being suppressed. 3. **Adaptive RNA-seq streaming:** Streams short-read and long-read RNA-seq libraries in waves (aligning with `HISAT2` for short reads and `minimap2` for long reads). After each wave, GeneLoop measures how often newly aligned reads still reveal unseen splice junctions in unresolved regions, prioritizing informative tissues or long-read libraries and halting redundant replicates once novel junction discovery drops below the stopping threshold. 4. **Transcript synthesis and biological refinement:** Assembles transcripts with `StringTie`, reconciles homology, deep-learning, and RNA-seq gene models into a unified annotation, scans splice gaps for short coding micro-exons (3-27 bp), separates intact single-exon genes (such as olfactory receptors and histones) from intronless retrocopy pseudogenes, and optionally annotates structural non-coding RNAs (`tRNA`, `rRNA`, `snRNA`, `snoRNA`) and `lncRNA` transcripts.
**Local Galaxy History files vs. public SRA/ENA accessions**
- **Galaxy History FASTQ files:** Under the default **Automatic** budget, GeneLoop reads up to 100% of your local FASTQ files (stopping earlier only when junction discovery has clearly converged), so small local datasets are never cut short. - **Galaxy History pre-aligned BAMs:** Skips read alignment and streaming entirely, extracting splice junctions and coverage directly from your coordinate-sorted BAMs. - **Public SRA/ENA accessions:** Under the default **Automatic** Logan mode, GeneLoop aligns compact pre-assembled transcript contigs from the public Logan archive whenever available (skipping raw short-read downloads for those runs) and falls back to adaptive raw short-read streaming (capped at 35% per library) only for runs absent from Logan. Choose **Logan contigs only** to bypass raw short-read streaming completely.
**What is saved in the state bundle**
The `.focaloop.tar.zst` archive stores compact locus, splice-junction, coverage-bin, and run-statistic summaries for archiving and auditing the annotation run. Note that GeneLoop state bundles are archival summaries and are not queried in **Focaloop Query** (which operates on **Focaloop ExpressionLoop** and **Focaloop VariationLoop** states).
-----
**Choosing an RNA-seq input mode**
| Your RNA-seq evidence | Mode to choose | What happens | |---|---|---| | Paired-end FASTQs in History | **Galaxy History paired-end short-read collection** | Filters redundant housekeeping reads and aligns with `HISAT2` | | Long-read cDNA or direct RNA in History | **Galaxy History long-read RNA-seq FASTQ files** | Aligns full-length isoforms with `minimap2` and assembles with `StringTie` | | Already-aligned BAM files in History | **Galaxy History pre-aligned RNA-seq BAM files** | Extracts splice junctions and coverage directly with no re-alignment | | Public SRA/ENA run accessions | **Public SRA/ENA run accessions** | Uses pre-assembled public contigs when available and streams raw reads adaptively | | No RNA-seq available | **None (seed only)** | Annotates from homology proteins and/or deep-learning prediction alone |
-----
**Inputs and manifest format**
- **Target genome assembly source:** Choose a built-in Galaxy genome (CVMFS cache, default), upload a eukaryotic FASTA assembly (`.fasta` or `.fasta.gz`) from your Galaxy History, or enter an NCBI assembly accession (`GCF_` or `GCA_` prefix) to download automatically. For mammals, select whether repeats are soft-masked in lowercase or unmasked so the right model weights are used. - **Related-species protein homology evidence:** Defaults to **Auto-fetch related RefSeq proteomes from NCBI**, which automatically discovers and merges annotated RefSeq proteomes from sister species in the same family or clade (`~15-80 MB`). You can also choose **Auto-fetch OrthoDB v12 clade proteins** (representative clade proteomes or full partitioned OrthoDB v12 packs), upload a custom **Protein FASTA from Galaxy History**, or choose **None**. - **Public SRA/ENA run manifest (for remote streaming):** Upload either a plain list of one run accession per line (`SRR`, `ERR`, or `DRR` prefix) or a tab-separated table:
| Column | Required | Description | |---|---|---| | `run_accession` | Yes | Public SRA/ENA run accession (`SRR`, `ERR`, or `DRR` prefix) | | `read_type` | Optional | `short` (Illumina) or `long` (PacBio Iso-Seq or ONT), defaults to `short` | | `organism` | Optional | Species name for cross-species metadata tracking |
Example TSV manifest:
``` run_accession read_type organism RUN_ACCESSION_1 short Example species RUN_ACCESSION_2 long Example species ```
-----
**Key parameters**
- **Gene-prediction compute strategy (`--mode`):** Leave on **Automatic**. It uses deep-learning prediction (Tiberius) whenever compatible weights are staged on the Galaxy server, and falls back cleanly to **Evidence-only** (protein homology + RNA-seq) when weights are absent. Note that if you run **Evidence-only** with neither proteins nor RNA-seq, no evidence is available to build gene models. - **Annotate structural non-coding RNAs:** Leave on **Automatic** so `tRNA`, `rRNA`, `snRNA`, and `snoRNA` models are added whenever Rfam databases are staged on the server and skipped gracefully otherwise. - **Rescue short micro-exons and filter processed retrocopies:** Enabled by default. Recovers 3-27 bp internal exons missed by standard splice aligners and labels processed intronless retrocopies as pseudogenes while protecting intact single-exon gene families. - **RNA-seq reading budget:** Leave on **Automatic**. Choose **Uncapped adaptive (up to 100%)** when you want remote libraries to stream past the 35% cap until splice discovery converges.
-----
**Outputs**
1. **Gene annotations (`annotation.gff3`):** Multi-biotype GFF3 annotation containing `protein_coding`, `lnc_RNA`, structural ncRNA (`tRNA`, `rRNA`, `snRNA`, `snoRNA`), and `pseudogene` features. Gene IDs begin with `GLC` when RNA-seq evidence was integrated or `GLA` in seed-only mode. 2. **Predicted proteins (`proteins.faa`):** Translated amino-acid sequences for all predicted coding transcripts. 3. **Transcript models (`transcripts.gtf`):** GTF annotation ready for downstream expression tools such as **Focaloop ExpressionLoop**. 4. **Annotation summary (`summary.tsv`):** Tabular metrics summarizing gene and biotype counts, streaming fractions, abundance-filter savings, and stopping reason (for example, `SEED_ONLY_NO_RNA` when run without RNA-seq). 5. **HTML report:** Interactive visual summary with gene-count cards, biotype and evidence charts, and per-library streaming statistics. 6. **State bundle (`geneloop_state.focaloop.tar.zst`):** Compact archival bundle recording loci, junctions, and alignment run statistics.
-----
**Tips and troubleshooting**
- **Running without deep-learning weights:** Under **Automatic**, GeneLoop detects missing Tiberius weights and switches smoothly to protein homology plus RNA-seq evidence. Always supply related-species proteins and/or RNA-seq when weights are not installed. - **Mammalian repeat masking mismatch:** Using soft-masked weights on an unmasked mammalian FASTA (or vice versa) degrades predictions. Check whether lowercase repeat bases appear in your FASTA before choosing. - **Custom Tiberius weights archive:** If you upload your own `.tar.gz` weights archive under **Advanced and benchmarking options**, GeneLoop extracts it automatically regardless of its Galaxy dataset filename.
